problems.field: participants.exclusions ('Same writers as S1 ... the human count is not printed'); also participants.who and paper_design_summary ('The same writers also played 24 rounds of rock-paper-scissors')
problems.form_value: Same writers as S1. Table 11 reports 811 (Balanced) and 779 (Unbalanced) observations and Table 12 reports 1,590, including 200 ChatGPT-4 games; the human count is not printed.
problems.source_says: Tables 11 and 12 regress on the player's type (ChatGPT-4 or Human), and ChatGPT-4 played 200 games in total. So the game sample holds 1,590 - 200 = 1,390 human players. Table 11's standard errors give the same answer: the ratio of the Human SE to the constant SE implies about 109-129 ChatGPT-4 games in Balanced and 79-94 in Unbalanced, so about 1,370 to 1,400 humans. That is 140 more people than the 1,250 writers analyzed in S1, and 69 more than the 1,321 complete responses in footnote 3. The text says every writer played the game, so the S1 writers are a subset of S4, not the same people. The human count is not printed, but it follows from printed numbers.
problems.quote: In total, 200 games were played in the different chats.
problems.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 10), Section 2.2; PDF p. 27 (printed p. 25), Table 11 and notes; PDF p. 28 (printed p. 26), Table 12 and notes

problems.form_value: Section 2.1.1 and Table 1 give 688, 253, and 309 writers (1,250, the number recruited). Footnote 3 says the authors received 702, 304, and 315 complete responses against preregistered targets of 700, 300, and 300. The paper does not explain the gap (14, 51, and 6 writers by arm) and gives no count at assignment.
problems.source_says: The form names only the 71 complete responses that are missing from the analysis. Every writer also played the game, and half of the participants played it first (footnote 7). About 1,390 humans appear in the game tables. So at least about 1,390 people started the experiment, and about 140 of them (10 percent) are not in the writing analysis: the 71 complete responses, plus about 69 people who played the game but are not among the 1,321 complete responses. The paper reports neither loss and gives no reason. The per-arm split of the 69 is unknown. The paper's own 'We recruited 1250 participants' conflicts with both 1,321 and 1,390, so the form should not present 1,250 as the number recruited without that flag. n_randomized = null stays right, because the paper prints no count at assignment.
problems.quote: The order of the tasks was randomized such that half of the participants started with the writing task and half started with the strategic task.

summary: The PDF supports S1's core counts: 1,250 writers analyzed (688, 253, and 309), one text each, and Table 4's tiers (169, 85, and 17 of 1,690 texts) show that all of them enter the rating analyses, so criterion 2 holds on S1 alone, with 997 people in the HumanPlusAI vs HumanBaseline contrast. The form misstates the game sample and understates attrition: Tables 11-12 (1,590 observations minus 200 ChatGPT-4 games) imply about 1,390 human players, so S4 is larger than S1 rather than 'the same writers', and about 140 people who took part are missing from the writing analysis, not only the 71 the form names.
